newsitem.title: GERMANY: Allianz targets global industrial insurance.
newsitem.headline: Allianz targets global industrial insurance.

text.p: Allianz Lebensversicherungs-AG Holding aims to increase its global industrial business to three billion marks premium income from the present two billion marks, by 1998 or 1999.

"We have a market share of between two and three percent. We want to double that in the foreseeable future," said Manfred Illner, president of Allianz Global Risk Management, in an interview with Reuters.
Already nearly all of Coca-Cola's bottling plants are insured by Allianz.
The deal with the producer of the quintessential American beverage is an example of how global insurance programmes should operate, said Illner.

"The leading company is Allianz Insurance in Burbank, California. All Allianz companies and offices worldwide provide the local service for the Coca-Cola account, including us here in Germany," he said.
The latest contract with Coca-Cola is for a global multi-line, multi-year programme.
Allianz is currently undergoing a fundamental reorganisation of its international industrial and commercial business to win more such lucrative deals.

Although international programmes form only a small part of Allianz's global 1996 income of 74.6 billion marks, and roughly half of its four billion marks total industrial business, Illner believes this sector has great potential -- especially as it is very profitable.
Illner sees U.S. insurer AIG , Winterthur , Zurich and Gerling as his major competitors on a global scale.

He said Lloyd's was not sufficiently organised to make an impact with such programmes, while others were not big enough. "We are among the top four in the world in this field. But we are sure that we are number one soon," he added.
